issues.problem: R11-01 is reported fixed, but codex research workers still run with no sandbox and no approvals. WORKER_PERMISSION_MODE='strict' only removes --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox; both the live adapter and agent_host_build_argv hard-code '--sandbox danger-full-access' for every mode, and codex exec is headless (it never asks for approval). The recorded need ('agent-host-exec.sh permissive mapping') names the wrong mapping: the strict mapping is the problem, in two files.

issues.problem: The strict claim gate still passes fabricated factual claims through new variants of the same R11-02 classes. (a) ENTITY_RE only recognises Capitalised-lowercase words, so all-caps acronyms (AWS, IBM, SAP) and camelCase brands (GitHub, GitLab, OpenAI) are not entities; the entity class then drops out as 'neutral' and a claim naming the wrong company scores 1.0. (b) Any factual sentence that also contains 'should'/'recommend' or 'might'/'may eventually' is classified recommendation/speculation and is exempt from --strict, even uncited. (c) Negation or verb swaps pass, which is inherent to lexical overlap and should at least be documented as a limit.
issues.evidence: REVF-H8a-probe/runs/fab2 (register-source + evidence_store add via '--json -' heredocs, extract_claims extract, verify_claim_support.py verify --dir . --strict): report '[1] AWS acquired GitHub in 2018 for 7.5 billion dollars [1].' with evidence 'Microsoft acquired GitHub in 2018 for 7.5 billion dollars' -> factual supported 1.0; uncited 'Acme raised 50 million dollars in 2023 and should be shortlisted.' -> recommendation unsupported (ignored by strict); 'The vendor does not guarantee zero downtime for enterprise customers [2].' vs 'The vendor guarantees zero downtime for all enterprise customers' -> supported 0.714. Gate output: status pass, factual_not_supported 0, exit=0. Unit probes: 'IBM acquired the company in 2019 for 34 billion' vs 'Oracle acquired ...' -> ('supported', 1.0); 'GitLab acquired the startup in 2021' vs 'GitHub acquired ...' -> ('supported', 0.758).
issues.suggested_fix: Extend entity extraction to acronyms and camelCase (e.g. r'\b[A-Z]{2,}[a-z]*\b', r'\b[A-Z][a-z]+[A-Z]\w*\b', plus lowercase tokens that match registered source/solution names). Classify by clause: a sentence that carries numbers, years or entities stays factual for the gate even with a hedge or recommendation clause (or strict also fails uncited recommendation/speculation that contains them). Document negation/antonym as a known limit of v1. Add tests for each variant.

Honest, reachable bibliographies fail verification; the only way past is --lenient, which turns every check off. FIX-BRIEF requires each new block to come with a test that the honest variant passes; there is none for real-world titles.
issues.evidence: REVF-H8a-probe/bin/vc_fp.py on runs/vc/report.md with every URL reported reachable: [1] Zhao et al. (2023) "A Survey of Large Language Models" arXiv URL -> 'Suspicious title pattern: Generic academic title pattern'; [2] Porter (1985) "Competitive Advantage: Creating and Sustaining Superior Performance" -> 'Anachronistic: pre-2000 (1985) citation mentioning modern AI terms' (substring 'ai' in 'Sustaining'); [3] "Pro Git Guide" -> 'Very generic short title'. issues.suggested_fix: Keep heuristic hits as warnings unless the entry also fails DOI/URL verification (or a DOI title mismatch), use word boundaries for the AI-term check ('\b(ai|llm|gpt|transformer)\b'), and do not hard-fail generic-but-real academic patterns. Add an honest-bibliography regression test with real titles like these.

issues.problem: Because workers now start with start_new_session=True, a terminal Ctrl-C (SIGINT to the foreground group) no longer reaches them. KeyboardInterrupt in the main thread then waits in ThreadPoolExecutor shutdown until each worker's timeout (600 s by default; cohort len*240+300 s). A second interrupt or SIGKILL of the dispatcher orphans the worker groups with no timeout left.
issues.evidence: REVF-H8a-probe/bin/ctrlc.py (fake cursor sleeping 25 s, timeout_sec=20), dispatcher started under setsid, then 'kill -INT -- -<dispatcher pgid>': 3 s later the worker (own pgid 13492) is still alive and the dispatcher is still running; output 'KeyboardInterrupt after 20.0' only when the worker timeout fired.
issues.suggested_fix: Track live Popen objects in a module-level set and, on KeyboardInterrupt/SIGTERM in the main thread (or atexit), killpg every tracked group before shutting the executor down; add a test.

issues.problem: SSRF residuals: the address check resolves the host and urllib resolves it again to connect (DNS-rebinding TOCTOU; the vetted address is not pinned). IPv6 NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96) and deprecated IPv4-compatible (::/96) encodings of 169.254.169.254 count as global.
issues.evidence: REVF-H8a-probe/bin/ssrf.py: 'http://[64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe]/ -> None', 'http://[::a9fe:a9fe]/ -> None'; every other form tried (decimal, hex, octal, short, mapped, userinfo, trailing dot, CGNAT, ULA) is blocked.
issues.suggested_fix: Connect to the vetted IP (custom HTTPConnection/HTTPSConnection with server_hostname set to the original host), and treat 64:ff9b::/96, 64:ff9b:1::/48 and ::/96 by checking the embedded IPv4 address.

issues.problem: Part of R11-17 is neither fixed nor disclosed: features with no evidence are still ticked by default (a dict without supported/present/evidence_ids, or a bare string). On a tie the SPA still renders 'Winner: <first>' above the tie note.
issues.suggested_fix: Require non-empty evidence_ids (or an explicit true) for a tick, or record the remaining gap in the disposition; on a tie, label the SPA heading 'Tie' instead of 'Winner'.

issues.problem: The GitHub token from GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN is sent as a regular request header, which urllib copies onto any redirect, including a cross-host one (CPython 3.13 HTTPRedirectHandler forwards every header except content-length/content-type).
issues.evidence: inspect.getsource(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler.redirect_request) on Python 3.13.16: 'newheaders = {k: v for k, v in req.headers.items() if k.lower() not in CONTENT_HEADERS}'. The search URL is SB's own api.github.com template, so the risk is low.
issues.suggested_fix: Use req.add_unredirected_header('Authorization', ...) or refuse redirects for the authenticated portal.
